source.title: Heavy-light decomposition and long-chain decomposition
source.primary_algorithm_description: For each vertex, select a child with maximum subtree height, inherit its depth-count state shifted by one, then merge every light-child depth vector.
source.independent_method: For each vertex, traverse its rooted subtree, count vertices at each distance, and choose the first distance with maximum count.
source.reuse: Mathematical algorithm only; clean-room ports and original fixtures.

input.encoding: [n,parent[1],...,parent[n-1]]; vertices are numbered in parent-before-child order and vertex 0 is the root
input.parent_rule: For each vertex v with 1 <= v < n, 0 <= parent[v] < v.

profile.dominant_depth: The smallest nonnegative distance d maximizing the number of descendants at exactly distance d, including the vertex itself at d=0.
profile.heavy_child: Child with greatest height, ties resolved by smaller vertex ID.
profile.arithmetic: Exact integer counts; all counts are at most 64.
profile.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) state for the primary long-chain DP; O(n^2) time and O(n) state for the independent traversal reference.

output.encoding: One signed i64 dominant depth per vertex, in vertex-ID order.

workspace.meaning: Eight fixed arrays of 64 signed 64-bit words account for 4,096 bytes in the widest ports; the remaining 4,096 bytes cover local scalar state, alignment, and ABI bookkeeping. The DP uses at most n active count slots in its 64-word fixed pool; output is caller-owned.
